script: Players who are working NORMAL JOBS, but SOMEHOW made it to the Premier League! Grant Holt got released by Carlisle United at 18 years old, and his football career looked completely over before it even started. So he got a job as a tire fitter and even spent time packing beetroots at a food factory near the docks in Barrow, all while still playing non-league football on the side for basically no money. But this is where his story starts to get ridiculous. Holt kept scoring goals that nobody in the professional game was watching, banging in 31 goals in 59 appearances for Barrow, which finally got him a move to Sheffield Wednesday. From there, he bounced to Rochdale, where he scored 42 goals, then Nottingham Forest, then Shrewsbury, where he won League Two Player of the Year. Every single stop, he kept proving people wrong, and then 2009, Norwich City signed him for about 400,000 pounds, but even Norwich had no idea what they were getting. His first game was a 7-1 loss against Colchester, and then he went on to score 30 goals that season and win Player of the Year. The next season, he did it again with 21 goals, another Player of the Year award, and Norwich got promoted to the Premier League. So at 30 years old, the former tire fitter and beetroot packer made his Premier League debut against Wigan Athletic, then scored 15 league goals that year, won his third straight Player of the Year award, and finished the season as the second-highest scoring Englishman in the Premier League, only behind Wayne Rooney.
